newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian inflation jumps to 1.2 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Russian inflation jumps to 1.2 pct in October.

text.p: Russia's monthly inflation rate quadrupled in October, official figures showed on Thursday, but economists said the rise was seasonal and did not signal the start of a new inflationary trend.
The State Statistics Committee said the monthly price rise in October was 1.2 percent after 0.3 percent in September.
In August prices actually fell 0.2 percent. The inflation rate has fallen fairly steadily since hitting 17.8 percent in January 1995.

"It would be wrong to think that this is a beginning of a new trend rather than the continuation of a slowdown with a monthly pick-up due to seasonal factors," said Al Breach, an economist with the London School of Economics.
"It is an autumn pick-up in service prices. Firms come back and hike prices after the summer recess."
The increase in the inflation rate reflects a traditional increase in prices for services and fruit and vegetables after a summer fall.
Last year was the first since the start of economic reforms in 1992 that Russia avoided a major acceleration in inflation in the late summer and autumn.
Money supply is not increasing at a rate which would suggest inflation problems ahead, Breach said.
The State Statistics Committee said that if current price trends continue, inflation over the whole of 1996 would be 21 percent.
The 1997 draft budget forecasts annual inflation next year at about 10 percent.
